statement: For finite compatible subsets T of a set L equipped with a reflexive symmetric compatibility relation, put C(T)={x outside T: x compatible with every t in T}. The marginal assertion is that C(T) determines T, and C(T)⊆C(T′) implies T′⊆T. The offered argument assumes compatibility of a selected t∈T′ with T, which the bare data do not ensure.
present_status: Not a theorem of arbitrary compatibility relations. Countermodel: L={a,b,c}, only a~c and b~c among distinct points. T={a}, T′={b} are compatible finite subsets with C(T)=C(T′)={c}. This refutes the assertion from the data then introduced, not a later fully axiomatized network.

statement: Proposed cutting axioms should recover boundary data from component equivalence relations, and all finite-cut equivalence relations from two-point cuts. This is established here only for the defined divisible ordered tronçon example, not for arbitrary networks.
present_status: The general-network anticipation has no complete axiom list here; the ordered-tronçon special case is C-SA21-3-007.

his_statement: Axiome ... partie finie modérée maximale ... L est discret
statement: The proposed discrete example has S0=P2(L), component equivalences equality on L\T, and empty boundaries. Proposed axioms additionally require every finite maximal compatible T to equal L with the discrete structure; every complement has finitely many components; refinement preserves component containment and restricts boundaries. These are defining requirements, not deductions from S0 alone.
present_status: The author explicitly calls the finiteness requirements perhaps provisional. For a discrete example, finite-component axiom Dec1 forces L finite.

statement: An ordered tronçon is a non-singleton poset, directed both upwards and downwards, dense between each comparable distinct pair, whose nonempty strict upper cones are downward directed and nonempty strict lower cones upward directed. For a finite chain t1<...<tn, declare components of C(T) to be the nonempty strict gaps and the two end rays; gap boundaries are their endpoints. Order reversal preserves this data. The endpoint types are segment (both extrema), half-interval (one), interval (neither).
computation: Gap count n+1 when there are no endpoints and all n cuts are internal; symbolic enumeration in code/computations.py.
present_status: Components are stipulated order components, not generally topological connected components. The literal closed brackets at scan11 conflict with C(T) excluding T.

his_statement: Une structure ... est connue ... b est strictement entre
statement: A non-singleton poset directed both ways is determined up to global reversal by its comparability relation and strict ternary betweenness B(a,b,c)↔a<b<c or c<b<a. If the order is dense between comparable distinct points, comparability itself is recovered by ∃c B(a,c,b). Fixing one oriented comparable pair a<b determines the order via common lower and upper bounds.
present_status: The proof uses global bidirectedness, not local cone conditions. Density is needed only to recover comparability from strict betweenness. The later Courcelle criterion matches reconstruction but not all arbitrary-cardinality conventions.

statement: In any poset, if x<y, u and v lie non-strictly between x and y, and u lies between x and v, then x≤u≤v≤y; equivalently the last condition can be replaced by v between u and y.
present_status: Independent proof: x<y and the first two betweenness assertions imply x≤u,v≤y; betweenness of u with x,v then forces u≤v. Degenerate equalities cause no exception.

statement: For a dense ordered tronçon and a three-point chain {a,b,c}, each two-point cut E selects the component X_E containing the third point. The middle point is the common endpoint of the unique pair E,E′ with X_E∩X_E′=∅. The other two intersections are nonempty by density. Thus pair compatibility and pair-cut component relations determine betweenness, hence the biorder.
computation: Symbolic three-gap calculation reproduced in code/computations.py.
present_status: Strict interval endpoints and density are essential; absent density two of the supposedly nonempty intersections can vanish.

his_statement: Il y a une plus grande T ... stable ... opposé
statement: There is a largest full class of non-singleton bidirected dense posets closed under taking nonempty strict upper and lower cones, and it is invariant under order reversal. The text uses this recursive closure description for tronçons. The existence follows by taking the union of all such classes; equivalence with the preceding first-order local definition requires checking iterated cone closure.
present_status: A class-theoretic construction, not a finiteness theorem. No universe convention specified.

statement: Two elementary intervals/rays/singletons in an ordered tronçon, with all their boundary points forming a chain, intersect in the empty set or another elementary interval/ray/singleton; the new designated boundary is contained in the union of old boundaries. The later version permits deleted endpoints.
present_status: The proof is finite endpoint comparison. The ordinary topological-frontier interpretation attempted at scan18 is withdrawn at scans23–26.

statement: A moderated subset presented as a finite ordered union of elementary tronçons separated by nonempty interstices has a unique such component decomposition. Scan19 first states this for disjoint closed compatible pieces; scan30 reformulates it for generalized pieces ordered by the strengthened separation relation ≪. Its designated frontier is their endpoint union with ambient endpoints omitted when locally included non-isolatedly.
present_status: The components and frontier are explicitly said not to be those of the canonical topology at scan30.

statement: Finite mutually compatible moderated subsets have intersection as meet and a moderated least upper bound as join, with boundaries contained in the union of input boundaries. Their generated compatible subalgebra is distributive. For compatible closed inputs the join is closed. The join need not be the set union in a non-total tronçon.
present_status: Scan20 gives double induction on component counts as proof plan; later Boolean-algebra axiom supplies distributivity.

statement: An arbitrary subset of a standard real interval need not have a least containing finite union of closed intervals and points: A={0,1,1/2,1/3,...}⊂[0,1] has none. Also [a,b]∨mod[b,c]=[a,c] may strictly contain the set union in a non-total tronçon; equality of the two rays about every b characterizes total order.
computation: Exact rational gap witness in code/computations.py.
present_status: No scan ambiguity affects the sequence example if 0 versus 1 is clarified: either displayed sequence has infinitely many isolated points accumulating at 0. For any proposed finite union containing A, its interval around the accumulation point contains a gap between successive 1/n; deleting a closedly separated open gap gives a smaller finite-union superset.

his_statement: Cmod(Y,X) ... plus petit ens. fermé modéré Z
statement: For closed moderated Y⊆X, the moderated complement Cmod(Y,X), consisting of x∈X\Y compatible with Y, has a least closed moderated hull Z⊆X; Z contains every moderated compatible closed piece disjoint from Y. If F is the designated frontier of Y relative to X, then F⊂Z has no isolated point of Z and Cmod(Y,X)=Cmod(F,Z).
present_status: Frontier here is the designated moderated frontier; ordinary topological identification is later retracted.

statement: For the poset of places of a topological ficelle with the canonical strict-interval topology, the specialization comparison is asserted to be reverse inclusion of the actual closed places: b∈cl{a} iff b⊇a. Hence singleton closures distinguish places and this example is T0.
present_status: The underlying topological-ficelle representation is needed; an arbitrary abstract tronçon is expressly left open next.

statement: Questions: is the canonical strict-interval topology of every abstract tronçon T0 or sober? If all its singletons are closed, must the tronçon be totally ordered? The pages assert that total orders yield a Hausdorff topology and closed order intervals/rays.
present_status: For L=R² with coordinatewise order, the strict-order topology is T0 (strict upper rays separate differing coordinates) but not T1: a=(0,0), b=(1,0) have special neighborhoods? This tentative example must not be used without a full check; see problems records for conservative formulation.

statement: Adjoining complements of closed order intervals/rays to the canonical topology is explored in hopes that closures of strict intervals/rays become their closed counterparts. The attempted local proof requires each elementary neighborhood of endpoint a to contain a whole initial interval ]a,ε[; the author says that requirement is false for a ficelle and abandons the topology. No counterexample to all three closure equalities themselves is fully established here.
present_status: Earlier attempt scan24; abandonment scan25. Do not turn the refuted sufficient condition into a proved refutation of the closure equations.

statement: The revised boundary of a closed elementary tronçon is its existing least/greatest elements, extended to endpoint-deleted pieces by remembering the closed hull. The representation T′=T\α with α⊆∂T is asserted unique, and the closed hull is least among closed elementary pieces containing T′. The relative frontier differs at ambient endpoints.
present_status: Scans25–27 replace crossed ordinary-frontier formulas. Some displayed ray-boundary identities omit ambient endpoints and cannot be literal absolute-boundary identities; registered as reading alarms.

statement: For two elementary nonempty pieces T<T′ (every element of T is below every element of T′), non-raccordement is equivalent to existence of a strict separating point, and to a unique nonempty interstitial elementary piece S with T<S<T′ adjoining both sides. Its endpoints are sup T and inf T′ in L, and S is precisely the strict separators. One-sided interstices are the sets of strict lower/upper bounds.
present_status: Endpoint inclusion determines whether a=b is allowed; density supplies a separator when a<b. Supremum of an open piece need not be an element of the piece: scan28 has a possible dropped ∂.

statement: The moderated complement of an n-component moderated set is the union of its n−1 internal interstices plus whichever exterior interstices exist. For n≥1, its component count is n−1+ell+r with ell,r∈{0,1}; hence the difference of component counts is at most one. It is the greatest moderated compatible subset disjoint from X.
computation: All four endpoint cases and empty-set exception in code/computations.py.
present_status: The count display uses n≥1. Empty X has complement L with one component, consistent with the difference bound but not the n−1+ell+r formula.

statement: Does the inclusion order on Mod(L) determine relative compatibility, perhaps by existence of a meet? The proposed iff is questioned, not asserted.
present_status: Meet existence alone fails as a general test in partial Boolean algebras: two noncompatible atoms can still have greatest lower bound 0. A counterexample to the particular Mod(L) requires preserving the tronçon realization, so none is claimed from this abstract example.

his_statement: engendrent une alg. de Boole ... anti-involution
statement: The moderated system is abstracted as a bounded poset with symmetric compatibility extending comparability, Boolean operations on every mutually compatible family, a compatible order-reversing complement, and a closure operation preserving compatible joins and compatibility. Boundary is cl X∧cl X′. In the tronçon model, empty moderated interior, equality with boundary, and finiteness of X are asserted equivalent.
present_status: These are not globally Boolean set operations. The finite-support conclusion is special to the one-dimensional moderated model.

statement: On a compatible Boolean subalgebra, symmetric difference is addition, meet is product, and join is X+Y−XY (equivalently X+Y+XY in characteristic two); X≤Y iff XY=X.
present_status: All four Boolean truth-table cases checked. The minus sign is not an error in characteristic two.

present_status: Proof checks each of seven axioms; scan35 top= X is a variable slip against fixed A. The theorem depends on the strengthened finite-compatible-family Boolean axiom.

statement: It is hoped that every clopen element of an abstract moderated algebra is compatible with every element. If so, clopens form a Boolean algebra; if this algebra is finite and 0≠1, its nonzero atoms are the components.
present_status: The universal compatibility clause is a separate hope, not proved from axioms1–7. Abstract counterexample with all elements declared closed in a non-Boolean partial Boolean algebra shows extra hypotheses are necessary; connection to a specific tronçon remains separate.

statement: For a moderated subset A=⋃T_i of a tronçon, its designated component pieces T_i are precisely components of its relative moderated algebra: each is relatively clopen and has no nontrivial clopen moderated subpiece. Their moderated closure is the associated closed elementary piece.
present_status: The author leaves an endpoint check in the closed-hull NB with an ellipsis, while the connectedness argument itself ends OK. This is not a statement about components of the canonical topology.

statement: For finitely many mutually compatible moderated sets, the page identifies components of the Boolean algebra they generate with all singleton boundary points and intervening open intervals/rays. With Boolean generation alone this is false: on R, one generator X=[0,1] generates {∅,X,X′,R}; its connected components include [0,1] intact, not {0},(0,1),{1}. The boundary-adapted interval algebra is a finer algebra containing the generators.
present_status: Hypotheses checked: R is non-singleton, dense, globally and locally bidirected; X is a single closed elementary tronçon; a singleton family is mutually compatible; its frontier is {0,1}. The correct refinement is C-SA21-3-027. Possible missing word must be checked on ink before editorial change.

statement: For finite chain S of designated endpoints in a tronçon, the atomic interval/singleton pieces determined by S generate a finite compatible Boolean algebra containing every moderated set whose boundary is in S. With k nonempty pieces its abstract Boolean cardinality is 2^k. Equality with the Boolean algebra generated by arbitrary original sets requires that their membership vectors separate the k pieces; without that condition it need not hold.
computation: Finite Boolean atom-membership check in code/computations.py.
present_status: Refinement supplied by this run; kept as target of refutation event, not attributed to Grothendieck.
